issues.problem: Contexts 1 (preparing a move) and 2 (sorting old documents, 骨の折れる作業) were generic labour-intensive tasks where the near-synonym 手がかかる / 手のかかる作業 would fit equally well.
issues.action: Rewrote both around strenuous, exhausting effort: cycling up a steep hill; walking around all day collecting signatures.

issues.problem: near diff and bad[0] why described 気を抜く as an 'unintended lapse'; 気を抜く is relaxing one's attention or tension and can be deliberate.
issues.action: Reworded both to 'relaxing one's attention or tension' / 'letting your attention slip'.

issues.problem: Context 6 (新人のころは手がかかった彼) could equally take 手を焼いた/手を焼かせた from the same set.
issues.action: Replaced with an easy-care flower (水やりに手がかからない), where 手を焼く does not fit.

issues.problem: Context 2 English 'Stop getting into gambling, especially with borrowed money' mistranslated 借金してまで.
issues.action: Changed to 'Don't go borrowing money to get into gambling.'

issues.problem: All stories are null; none of these body-part 慣用句 has a well-established origin story that can be stated with certainty.
